long_biography.plain_text:
Lorina was a small, century-old lemonade maker when Jean-Pierre Barjon acquired it in the mid-1990s. He kept his executive job in the computer trade at first, working on the drinks business in evenings and at weekends. Once he committed full time, he refreshed the brand's packaging and distribution and developed overseas markets. The company was sold to Royal Unibrew in 2018, ending his role at the producer he had built up.

Horses became the other enduring centre of Barjon's life. His trotter Meaulnes du Corta won the Prix d'Amérique, and his racing and breeding stable has remained active across the sport. As president of the Société du Trotteur Français, he has also helped direct the institutions behind French harness racing.

Lorina was a small, century-old lemonade maker when Jean-Pierre Barjon acquired it in the mid-1990s. Once he committed full time, he refreshed the brand's packaging and distribution and developed overseas markets. The company was sold to Royal Unibrew in 2018, ending his role at the producer he had built up.

Horses became the other enduring centre of Barjon's life. His trotter Meaulnes du Corta won the Prix d'Amérique, and his racing and breeding stable has remained active across the sport. As president of the Société du Trotteur Français, he has also helped direct the institutions behind French harness racing.
